limitations: Reported job time and proof-request time have different boundaries.
Their difference does not isolate a particular overhead or critical path.
Device stage medians are observations, not a throughput qualification.
No deadline, timing approval, resource allowance, or failed candidate was changed.
Samples locate changes within intervals; transient peaks can occur between samples.
Cumulative memory.peak was not reset and is not a trial-specific peak.
Child cgroups may disappear before their final sample; service receipts remain authoritative.
Synthetic compaction improves about 7.2x in device time and 3.6x in wall time; this does not measure delivered throughput.
The first isolated diagnostic rejected compiler local-memory overhead; its successor records 16388 bytes for the 16384-byte array.
The first CLI images omitted established host/wide feature profiles; CPU setup rejected them before GPU proving. Corrected images match the prior production profiles.
The new kernel passed production GPU qualification and calibration, but the native workflow hit a 16-second handoff timeout.
The original workflow had more than 120 seconds remaining; the phase dispatch window had under one second left after native sealing.
No final aggregate root or native block was produced, and the sealed failed candidate remains terminal.
A planned handoff deferral must be admitted before callback start, retain both original clocks, and never restart a failed handoff.
